activity.title: Hands-On Lab: Build and Defend a Bounded Agent Workflow
instructions: Step 1: Clone the reference repository and configure your local OpenAI/Foundry endpoint environment variables.
Step 2: Implement the circuit breaker middleware to enforce a hard maximum of 5 tool iterations.
Step 3: Execute the failure injection test script (`npm run test:inject-failures`) and observe how the system catches runaway loops.
Step 4: Refactor the tool handler to enforce read-only execution permissions for unauthenticated users.
evidence: Working code implementation showing the bounded execution wrapper.
Terminal execution logs proving that runaway iterations tripped the circuit breaker with exit code 0.
A completed risk assessment matrix documenting residual failure modes.

questions.prompt: What is the primary architectural purpose of a circuit breaker in an autonomous agent loop?

options.text: To increase the context window limit of the underlying frontier model.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Circuit breakers do not alter context window sizes; they limit execution steps.

options.text: To bound execution steps and prevent runaway loops, runaway spend, and infinite retries.
options.feedback: Correct! Circuit breakers ensure that runaway execution loops terminate safely after a predefined threshold.

options.text: To bypass user authentication for faster tool invocation.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Circuit breakers enforce security boundaries rather than bypassing them.
